A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SketchTune study. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial formatting changes and appendix reordering.

before.justification: V2 reports original SketchTune fine-tuning accuracies, perplexities, weight-update approximation analyses and GPU efficiency measurements, including additional results in its appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds MT-Bench evaluation, rank statistics, model-sketching scalability measurements and answer-extraction comparisons.

M1.justification: The weighted-k-means sketching, sequential error compensation, grouping, frozen mappings, sketch fine-tuning and CUDA procedures remain unchanged. Expanded explanations and corrected gradient expressions do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V3 adds Alpaca-GPT4 training and MT-Bench evaluation with 80 multi-turn questions across eight categories, extending the existing instruction-following coverage. The earlier math, commonsense, language-modeling and Alpaca evaluations remain.

E2.justification: V3 adds SpIEL and SMT(Best) as evaluated commonsense comparators in Table 11, using cited baseline results. The earlier comparator sets remain; the new MT-Bench comparison uses the already represented full fine-tuning and S2FT methods.

E3.justification: V3 introduces Mistral-7B instruction tuning with GPT-4o MT-Bench scoring, regex-versus-o3-mini evaluation across LoRA/DoRA ranks 2–16, and A100 sketching measurements on 3B, 8B and 70B models. It also changes the reported Llama-3-8B commonsense learning rate from 3×10^-5 to 2×10^-5 (v2 Table 5; v3 Table 8), without establishing that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds substantive diagnostics: required rank versus explained variance in Figure 1, sensitivity of math accuracy to answer extraction in Appendix L, and sketching scalability through 70B parameters in Appendix G. These address additional questions beyond the retained approximation-error and efficiency analyses.

E5.justification: V3 explicitly reports standard deviations and shaded variability bands for the new required-rank analysis. The timing protocol still averages ten runs with ten warmup steps; no increase in repeated training runs or seeds is reported.

E6.justification: V3 adds rank statistics, resource measurements and Tables 3, 11 and 13 results. MT-Bench averages are 6.36 for SketchTune, 5.27 for S2FT and 4.64 for full fine-tuning; the sparse comparison also shows SMT slightly ahead on Llama-3-8B, 87.2 versus 87.0. Additional math scores depend on the answer extractor. Matched earlier benchmark, efficiency and appendix results retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Equation 6 and the detailed gradient formula in Appendix E correct reversed derivatives to express gradients of loss with respect to weights. The central theorem, assumptions and proof remain unchanged, with the proof moved from Appendix J to Appendix F.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of unified compression and adaptation, avoiding low-rank constraints and separate adapter computation, and competitive accuracy with smaller models. Naming Mistral reflects additional validation rather than a redefinition of these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix L newly explains how last-number regex extraction can misclassify correct mathematical responses and motivates LLM-based extraction. V3 also discusses sketching as a one-time preprocessing cost and explicitly motivates GPR=4 as a memory–accuracy tradeoff.

D1.justification: V3 adds a SketchTune code repository pointer, Mistral training hyperparameters, and hardware/configuration details for the new scalability measurements. It also explicitly discloses the existing main math evaluation's last-number regex extraction, which v2 described only as answer extraction.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a distinction between prior random sketching for training from scratch and SketchTune's post-training compression, including an 'among the first' positioning statement. References expand to additional sketching, compression, model and sparse-adapter work; the overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites the motivation and mapping explanations, reorganizes the appendices, adopts author-year citations, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: A two-column conference format replaces the single-column main text and references, substantially changing typography, sizing and float placement. Figure 1 is reorganized from four horizontal panels into six panels, and four new tables present the added evaluations and measurements.

improvement.justification: The added rank and answer-extraction diagnostics, broader comparisons, resource measurements, code-access information and gradient corrections improve evidential support and reproducibility. These are incremental gains over v2's already extensive method documentation, theory and empirical evaluation.
